canonical_question: Could the 'basically the same' hardness at 300 K and 600 K be an artifact of the time scale of the simulation?

question_variants.question: Could the 'basically the same' hardness at 300 K and 600 K be an artifact of the time scale of the simulation?
question_variants.resolution_summary: The text states that hardness was 'basically the same' at 300 K and 600 K, but it does not explicitly address whether this is an artifact of the simulation time scale. It attributes changes in mechanical properties to dislocation density and lattice disorder.

answers.answer: The document confirms that hardnesses were basically the same at 300 K and 600 K, but does not attribute this to simulation time scale artifacts. Instead, it links mechanical property changes to lattice disorder and dislocation density variations.
answers.measurement_outcome: Hardnesses were basically the same at 300 K and 600 K
answers.mechanism: Changes in dislocation density and lattice disorder with temperature
answers.boundary_limitation: Results derived from molecular dynamics simulation
evidence_spans: In this study, the wear resistance of the FeNiCrCoCu high entropy alloy coating was systematically analyzed by the molecular dynamics method.
The friction and nanoindentation simulation of this coating material were carried out by controlling the ambient temperature.

The results show that with the increase of temperature, the disorder of the lattice structure increases, which leads to an increase of the tangential force and friction coefficient in the friction process.
